The chord-to-radius ratio (c/R) has a significant impact on cross-flow turbine performance.
Virtual camber and incidence effects are important in cross-flow turbine optimization.
The conformal transformation method is used to quantify virtual camber and incidence.
Higher c/R values result in higher performance, particularly at lower Reynolds numbers.
The optimal preset pitch angle is strongly dependent on c/R.
Positive camber increases upstream lift, while negative camber reduces downstream losses.
Flow curvature has a noticeable effect on performance.
The experimental datasets analyzed in this paper were collected using the same experimental setup and under similar flow conditions.
The time-averaged power coefficient (Cp) is used to characterize overall turbine performance.
The power coefficient (Cp) is defined as the ratio of mechanical work power to kinetic power in the flow.
The Reynolds number (ReD) is used to characterize the flow regime.
The Froude number (Frh) is used to characterize the flow regime.
The blockage ratio is approximately 11% across all tests.
The blade height and outermost diameter are held constant at 23.4 cm and 17.2 cm, respectively.
The chord length and blade preset pitch are varied across the experiments.
The tip-speed ratio is swept across a range of values for each turbine configuration.
Data are logged using MATLAB at a sample frequency of 1 kHz.
The experiments are conducted in a recirculating water flume at the University of Washington.
The free stream velocity is 1.1 m/s, and the dynamic depth is 0.48 m.
The temperature is 38.9 ± 0.1°C, and the turbulence intensity is 2-4%.
